subject: Request: SLA exception for marketplace listing - branding & claims review
messages:
From: Ruth Kim <r.kim@acmeanalytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: MarketplaceOps <marketplace-ops@aws-partner.com>
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing support SLA & branding details (initial)

Hi Jasmine / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — Acme's product team is excited to move forward with a marketplace listing on AWS and we'd like to align on two items before we kick off the listing preflight:

1) Support SLA window: Our legal/procurement team needs confirmation of Redwood's support hours for marketplace listings. Acme's customers require a 24x7 support option for high-availability customers; can Redwood support a 24x7 Tier for the listing or would that require an exception / additional billing?

2) Branding and claims: We have a product page copy that references 99.9% uptime and an integration with SSO. We need Redwood's approval on brand usage and to confirm whether the uptime claim aligns with Redwood's verified SLA language (we can't publish claims that exceed what Redwood is contractually guaranteeing).

I attached a draft SLA and a copy of our planned marketplace listing blurb for your review. Could you let me know the path to get an exception approved (if needed) and approximate turnaround time? We are aiming for listing submission the week of 26 May.

Thanks,
Ruth
Ruth Kim
Head of Partnerships, Acme Analytics
r.kim@acmeanalytics.com

Attachment: ACME_SLA_Draft.pdf
From: jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com
To: Ruth Kim <r.kim@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 17 May 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing support SLA & branding details (initial)

Hi Ruth — thanks for the clear summary and the files. Looping in Ben (partner ops) and Marissa (co-sell / listings) to get procurement & brand signoff.

Quick answers up front:
- Support window: Our standard marketplace listing includes business-hours support (M-F 9-5 PT) for self-serve customers. We offer an add-on 24x7 incident routing for enterprise customers through Dedicated/Managed plans — this is doable but requires a small uplift and an SLA exception approval for the public listing.
- Uptime/claims: We can co-author copy that references our verified SLA language. We cannot approve "99.9% uptime" on behalf of Redwood in a public listing unless the customer purchases the dedicated capacity plan that backs that level of commitment. We can, however, include a statement like "Backed by Redwood Inference SLAs for Dedicated customers" and link to the SLA page.

Questions for you before we move to the exception workflow:
- Will Acme require the 24x7 option be visible on the public marketplace tile (e.g., pricing/plan selector) or only available via sales contract?
- Is the uptime claim required on the listing, or can it be moved to a footnote linking to the SLA terms?

Ben / Marissa — can you confirm the procurement/exception process and approximate lead time? I flagged this as time-sensitive (target submission week of 26 May).

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Partner Programs, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com

Thanks for the context, Jasmine. Quick notes from listings & legal preflight POV: 

- Exception path: We can approve a public-facing note that advertises "Enterprise support available" with a link to a contact form, rather than listing explicit 24x7 hours on the tile. That avoids misrepresenting our default bus-hours coverage. If Acme needs the 24x7 tag directly visible, we require:
  * Procurement signoff (vendor contract addendum)
  * Product operations test plan (to ensure routing)
  * Sales uplift (we usually capture as a pre-approved surcharge)

- Uptime claim: Legal says we cannot sign off on "99.9%" unless we ship Dedicated capacity and the customer is under the corresponding SLA. Suggest the following copy variants: 
  a) "High-availability offering with Redwood-backed SLA for Dedicated customers" (preferred)
  b) If they insist, include: "99.9% uptime for Dedicated deployments — contact sales for details" (requires evidence in the listing notes)

- Evidence & listing attachments: We should receive the ACME_SLA_Draft.pdf and a redlined copy of their marketplace blurb. I reviewed the draft and left inline comments in listing_brand_guidelines_v2.docx (attached).

Ben — can you confirm how fast procurement can turn the addendum? Typical SLA exceptions for marketplace tiles have been ~7-10 business days once procurement has a signed statement of work. We may be able to expedite to 3 business days if we treat this as a channel co-sell priority.

Marissa Cole
Head of Listings & Co-sell, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: listing_brand_guidelines_v2.docx

Hi Ruth — looping back with a concrete path and next steps so we can hit your 26 May target.

What Redwood can do now:
- Listing copy: We will publish the tile with the phrasing: "High-availability offering — enterprise SLA available for Dedicated customers. Contact sales for details." That avoids an explicit uptime claim while signalling the enterprise option.
- 24x7 visibility: We can surface a "24x7 support" badge only if Acme signs the addendum. Otherwise it remains an option via sales contract.
- Timeline: If Acme signs the attached procurement addendum and returns it by EOD 21 May, Listings team will prioritize final QA and push to staging by 23 May. Public submission to the AWS marketplace would follow after final legal check (target 26 May).

Action items for Acme:
1) Confirm whether 24x7 needs to be visible on the tile or only available via sales.
2) If visible, sign and return the attached addendum (DocuSign link below) by EOD 21 May.
3) Accept our recommended copy variant (we've attached a redline).
